Here's the function.

```python
import re

_EMAIL_RE = re.compile(
    r"^[a-zA-Z0-9!#$%&'*+/=?^_`{|}~-]+"
    r"(?:\.[a-zA-Z0-9!#$%&'*+/=?^_`{|}~-]+)*"
    r"@"
    r"(?:[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?\.)+"
    r"[a-zA-Z]{2,63}$"
)


def is_valid_email(address: str) -> bool:
    """Return True if `address` has a valid email format."""
    if not isinstance(address, str) or len(address) > 254:
        return False
    local, sep, _domain = address.rpartition("@")
    if not sep or len(local) > 64:
        return False
    return _EMAIL_RE.match(address) is not None
```

I ran it on 16 addresses, 4 good and 12 bad. All came out right.

This checks the shape only. To know an address really receives mail, send it a confirmation link.
